notes:
Account summary: Amber Skyline Reserve (high-traffic ecommerce marketplace). Considering Redwood Dedicated + Private control plane for customer personalization and real-time recommendation service. Primary concern is predictable unit economics at peak holiday traffic and tight p95 latency for short chat sessions. Procurement team is focused on hard throughput guarantees and measurable SLA credits.

Key ask from Amber: minimum sustained tokens/sec across reserved pool, explicit concurrency caps per model to avoid noisy neighbor issues, and clear burst policy with defined billing and failover. They want a guaranteed baseline for capacity planning and an option to autoscale with capped bursts for promotion windows.

Quote from CTO: "We need absolute predictability for Black Friday — if your reserved pool doesn't deliver the minima we agree, it needs to be measurable and remediated automatically." -- paraphrase from 2025-09-18 meeting.

POC notes: SE (Naomi) proposed a 24-hour sustained throughput run against a representative request mix (30% personalization scoring, 50% short chat, 20% reranking) with synthetic traffic and live shadowed requests to gauge KV cache hit-rate. Acceptance criteria defined in SLA draft: sustained min tokens/sec, p95 generation latency <= 180ms for 64-token responses, and no more than 1% token failure rate over 24h.

Commercial negotiation items: reserved GPU count equivalence (we proposed 8x A100-v4 equiv), sustained baseline 275k tokens/sec aggregate, concurrency cap of 120 concurrent generation streams across the pool, burst allowance up to 2x sustained for 15 minutes per hour with soft throttling thereafter, and financial credits (5% monthly credit per SLA miss tiered). Amber pushes for stricter p95 (150ms) and higher baseline (320k tokens/sec) for peak windows.

Security/compliance: requires SOC2 attestation, encrypted-at-rest keys managed by their KMS, audit logs forwarded to their SIEM, and EU data residency for EU-origin traffic (hybrid routing).

Other misc: referenced Redwood pricing deck v3, early draft of SLA (drive link), and internal legal redline (thread).

throughput_requirements: Amber requests a guaranteed sustained baseline of 275000 tokens/sec across the reserved Dedicated pool (target for negotiation: 275k-320k). Concurrency cap requested by Redwood: initial proposal 120 concurrent streams, Amber asking for per-model caps to isolate noisy models (proposal: 80 per-model soft cap with pool-level hard cap 120). Burst policy proposed: allow up to 2x sustained throughput for 15 minutes per 60-minute window; bursts beyond that subject to throttling and overage billing. Measurement window: 5-minute sliding windows aggregated hourly for SLA evaluation.
negotiation_summary: Open items: p95 latency target (Amber wants 150ms p95 for typical 64-token responses; Redwood proposes 180ms with cache tuning), baseline tokens/sec (Redwood proposed 275k; Amber pushes toward 320k for holiday peaks), GPU equivalence mapping (dispute on A100v4 vs latest config), and burst billing clarifications (flat cap vs consumption-based). Agreed items: 24h POC with defined acceptance criteria, VPC private control plane requirement, SOC2 + KMS requirements, and initial reserved capacity term of 12 months with quarterly review. Next commercial step: finalize SLA doc and produce SOW and pricing appendix for exec sign-off.
poc_details: 24h sustained run with mixed traffic (30/50/20 split)
Instrumentation: token-level cost, p95/p99 latencies, cache hit rate, failure rate logging

sla_penalty_structure: Tiered credit model proposed: 5% monthly credit for first-level breach (1-2% below baseline), 15% for severe breach (2-5%), 30% for catastrophic (>5%). Latency breaches handled via remediation playbook and 3% credit per missed p95 window after 3 strikes. Credits capped at 50% per month. Legal to negotiate caps and force majeure carveouts.
commercial_terms_highlights: 12-month reserved term (auto-renew), option to convert reserved units to committed burst credits, monthly true-up for sustained overage, price lock for first 12 months, milestone-based SOW payments tied to POC acceptance.
reliability_expectations: Automatic fallback routing to compatible model variants if primary model exceeds latency SLO; Redwood to provide tracing hooks and token-level diagnostics. Amber requires runbooks and a 4-hour on-call SLA for critical incidents during peak windows.
